profile.name: Vaishnavi Khindkar
profile.degree_line: MS in Computer Vision at Carnegie Mellon University's Robotics Institute (graduating December 2026)
profile.experience_line: ~5 years of research experience in computer vision, 3D reconstruction, and generative AI
profile.work_authorization: I'm on an F-1 visa and will be authorized to work in the US on OPT after graduating in December 2026. I will require visa sponsorship in the future.

evidence.label: Sync Labs VLM quality control
evidence.short: fine-tuned a 27B VLM for AI-video quality control at Sync Labs (macro-F1 0.19→0.49)
evidence.text: This summer, as an ML Engineering intern at Sync Labs, I built an automated visual quality-control system for AI lip-sync video: a fine-tuned vision-language model judges appearance defects while classical CV (sharpness, plate-difference maps, optical flow) handles geometry and motion. I fine-tuned Qwen 3.6-27B with a single multi-task LoRA adapter (124M parameters) on 8×H200 GPUs, raising QC macro-F1 from 0.19 to 0.49 and beating GPT-5.6-sol zero-shot (0.30).

evidence.label: ECCV 2026 detector diagnosis
evidence.short: co-authored ECCV 2026 work using generative models to diagnose object detectors
evidence.text: I'm a co-author on an ECCV 2026 paper that turns foundation image generative models (Imagen-3) into a diagnostic tool for aerial object detectors, enabling fine-grained failure analysis and up to 11% AP50 gains.

evidence.label: Slot4D 4D reconstruction (capstone)
evidence.short: built Slot4D, an object-centric 4D reconstruction head on VGGT (up to 4× better surface reconstruction)
evidence.text: My CMU capstone, Slot4D, adds an adaptive slot-attention head over VGGT features that decomposes scenes into object slots and masks; slot-conditioned refinement gives up to 4× better surface reconstruction on CO3D, ScanNet, and Virtual KITTI, and I'm extending it to streaming 4D.

evidence.label: Reward-tilted sampling (Risteski)
evidence.short: research reward-tilted sampling for generative models with Prof. Andrej Risteski
evidence.text: As a Graduate Research Fellow with Prof. Andrej Risteski in CMU's Machine Learning Department, I study reward-tilted sampling: principled lift-and-tilt methods for steering generative models toward target distributions under complex, indefinite rewards.

evidence.label: Bhashini Triton deployment
evidence.short: deployed OCR for 22 languages on NVIDIA Triton at real-time latency
evidence.text: At Bhashini (Government of India), I containerized OCR models with Docker and deployed them on NVIDIA Triton at real-time latency (0.11 s printed, 0.051 s handwritten) across 22 Indian languages.

evidence.label: CVIT research (IROS, WACV, patent)
evidence.short: led pedestrian-intent research (IROS 2024) and domain-adaptive detection (WACV 2022)
evidence.text: Over three years as a Jr. Research Scientist at CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, I led MindReaD, reason-enriched pedestrian intent estimation (IROS 2024; new PIE++ dataset, +5.6% accuracy and +7% F1 over baselines), and developed ILLUME, a self-attention-based domain-adaptive object detector (WACV 2022). I also hold a granted US patent on adaptive object detection.

evidence.label: Cross-resolution Gaussian Splatting
evidence.short: built a cross-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline
evidence.text: With Prof. Shubham Tulsiani, I designed a cross-resolution 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline that fuses heterogeneous image sources, with detail-preserving densification for high-fidelity reconstruction.

evidence.label: Robot pose estimation
evidence.short: built single-view robot pose estimation with sim-to-real transfer
evidence.text: With Prof. Jun-Yan Zhu, I built a single-view robot pose and keypoint estimation pipeline with synthetic-to-real transfer and domain randomization for unseen robot types.

evidence.label: Modern C++
evidence.text: I write Modern C++ (14/17/20) as well as Python.
